---
title: "Current vs Usual"
subtitle: "How do today's buoy conditions compare to the past five years?"
author: "USGS / SECOORA ERDDAP"
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: cosmo
    css: styles.css
    nav-buttons:
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/usf-imars/fl-bay-usgs-buoy-explorer
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r setup}
#| output: false

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(htmltools)
library(leaflet)
library(scales)

source("R/fetch_ndbc_history.R")
source("R/fetch_ndbc_observations.R")
source("R/plot_ndbc_context.R")
source("R/plot_ndbc_field.R")
source("R/load_field_data.R")

lookback_years <- 5
lookback_days <- lookback_years * 365

history_raw <- fetch_ndbc_network_history(lookback_days = lookback_days)
data_as_of <- fetch_ndbc_erddap_end_time()
data_as_of_label <- format_ndbc_time(data_as_of)
report_time <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z", tz = ndbc_display_tz)

sal_history <- prepare_ndbc_history(history_raw$salinity, "salinity")
temp_history <- prepare_ndbc_history(history_raw$temperature, "temperature")

sal_latest <- latest_ndbc_readings(sal_history, "salinity")
temp_latest <- latest_ndbc_readings(temp_history, "temperature")

sal_daily <- network_daily_means(sal_history, "salinity")
temp_daily <- network_daily_means(temp_history, "temperature")

sal_clim <- doy_climatology(sal_history, "salinity")
temp_clim <- doy_climatology(temp_history, "temperature")

sal_network_ctx <- network_daily_context(sal_daily, sal_clim, "salinity", lookback_years)
temp_network_ctx <- network_daily_context(temp_daily, temp_clim, "temperature", lookback_years)

sal_qc_label <- ndbc_qc_label("salinity")
temp_qc_label <- ndbc_qc_label("temperature")

sal_ndbc <- fetch_ndbc_hourly_snapshots(
  param = "sea_water_practical_salinity",
  value_col = "salinity"
)
temp_ndbc <- fetch_ndbc_hourly_snapshots(
  param = "sea_water_temperature",
  value_col = "temperature"
)

ref_date_label <- format(sal_ndbc$reference_date, "%Y-%m-%d")

salinity_fields <- interpolate_or_load_fields(
  sal_ndbc$snapshots,
  value_col = "salinity"
)
temperature_fields <- interpolate_or_load_fields(
  temp_ndbc$snapshots,
  value_col = "temperature"
)

salinity_palette <- c(
  "#2166ac", "#67a9cf", "#d1e5f0",
  "#fddbc7", "#ef8a62", "#b2182b"
)
temperature_palette <- c(
  "#313695", "#74add1", "#abd9e9",
  "#fee090", "#f46d43", "#a50026"
)

sal_field_range <- field_value_range(salinity_fields, "salinity")
temp_field_range <- field_value_range(temperature_fields, "temperature")
sal_range <- sal_field_range
temp_range <- temp_field_range
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="dashboard"}
**Usual** = the 10th–90th percentile of the past **`r lookback_years` years** of readings. Data from [SECOORA ERDDAP](https://erddap.secoora.org/erddap/index.html). **Report:** `r report_time` · **Latest data:** `r data_as_of_label`
:::

# Overview

## Row {height=35%}

::: {.card title="Network mean salinity"}
`r format_network_context(sal_network_ctx, "PSU")`
:::

::: {.card title="Network mean temperature"}
`r format_network_context(temp_network_ctx, "°C")`
:::

## Row {height=40%}

::: {.card title="How to read this dashboard"}
Distribution plots show the QC-filtered **`r lookback_years`-year** record (all buoys pooled), with each buoy's latest reading marked against that history. Interpolated maps show **DIVAnd** hourly fields on `r ref_date_label` for the variable on each page.

Click the **Salinity** or **Temperature** tabs in the top right to see the distribution, interpolated maps, and yearly trend for each variable.

Outliers and sentinel values are removed before analysis (salinity `r sal_qc_label` PSU; temperature `r temp_qc_label` °C).
:::

# Salinity

## Row {height=55%}

```{r sal-distribution}
#| title: Salinity distribution (past `r lookback_years` years)
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 5

if (nrow(sal_history) == 0) {
  stop("No salinity history returned from ERDDAP.")
}

plot_context_distribution(
  sal_history,
  sal_latest,
  value_col = "salinity",
  title = sprintf("Salinity distribution (past %d years)", lookback_years),
  unit = "Salinity (PSU)"
)
```

::: {.card title="How to interpret these charts"}
The **distribution** (left) is the QC-filtered salinity record for all buoys over the past `r lookback_years` years. The gray dashed lines mark the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles of that history. The orange lines mark each buoy's latest reading: the closer a line sits to either edge of the histogram, the more unusual that buoy's current salinity is for this time of year.

Below, the interpolated maps show how salinity varies across the bay at four times on `r ref_date_label`, and **Network mean by year** compares this year's daily average (orange) against every prior year (thin black lines) and the climatological median band.
:::

## Row {height=50%}

### Column {width=50%} {.tabset}

```{r sal-field-06}
#| title: 06:00 ET
#| padding: 0px

plot_ndbc_hour_field(
  salinity_fields[[1]],
  value_col = "salinity",
  legend_title = "Salinity (PSU)",
  popup_suffix = " PSU",
  palette = salinity_palette,
  value_range = sal_range
)
```


### Column {width=50%}

```{r sal-network-year}
#| title: Network mean by year
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 4.5

plot_network_mean_by_year(
  sal_daily,
  sal_clim,
  title = "Network mean salinity by year",
  unit = "Salinity (PSU)",
  lookback_years = lookback_years
)
```

# Temperature

## Row {height=55%}

```{r temp-distribution}
#| title: Temperature distribution (past `r lookback_years` years)
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 5

if (nrow(temp_history) == 0) {
  stop("No temperature history returned from ERDDAP.")
}

plot_context_distribution(
  temp_history,
  temp_latest,
  value_col = "temperature",
  title = sprintf("Temperature distribution (past %d years)", lookback_years),
  unit = "Temperature (°C)"
)
```

::: {.card title="How to interpret these charts"}
The **distribution** (left) is the QC-filtered temperature record for all buoys over the past `r lookback_years` years. The gray dashed lines mark the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles of that history. The orange lines mark each buoy's latest reading: the closer a line sits to either edge of the histogram, the more unusual that buoy's current temperature is for this time of year.

Below, the interpolated maps show how temperature varies across the bay at four times on `r ref_date_label`, and **Network mean by year** compares this year's daily average (orange) against every prior year (thin black lines) and the climatological median band.
:::
